title: On Patmos (Revelation 1:9–20)
hookLine: John, exiled, sees the risen Christ among lampstands: fear not
carry: fear not, I am the first

lines: A VOICE LIKE A TRUMPET, BEHIND HIM.
cards: "I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation." That's how the man who saw all this introduces himself. Not as a prophet, not as a bishop.
Your brother. Your companion in the hard part. Then he says where he is: "in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ."
An island, sea on every side. Tradition says he'd been banished. It's the Lord's day, he's in the Spirit, and from behind him comes a voice loud as a trumpet.
Today, the moment John turns around.

teach.h: HE TURNS TO SEE A VOICE.
teach.b: First, he turns to see a voice. That's how the King James puts it: "And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks."
Lampstands, standing in the dark, and in the midst of them "one like unto the Son of man." Second, the figure.
John piles up pictures, because ordinary words won't hold it. Hair white as wool, white as snow. Eyes like a flame of fire.
Feet like polished brass glowing in a furnace. A voice like many waters. Seven stars in his right hand.
A sharp two-edged sword from his mouth. A face like the sun at full strength. Not meant to be drawn like a photo; meant to overwhelm.
Third, what John does, and what Christ does. "When I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead."
Then the tender part: "he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last." The hand that holds the stars is laid on a frightened man.
"I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore."

Fourth, the vision explains itself: "the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches." So the first thing Revelation unveils about the risen Christ is where he stands. Not far off in the sky.
In the midst of the churches, among the small, flickering lamps, with all their trouble. Present, not distant.

how: Christians read this vision of the risen Christ in personal prayer and in church, and its words 'fear not; I am the first and the last' are read in times of grief and trouble.

games.q: you're on Patmos, in the Spirit on the Lord's day. a voice like a trumpet speaks behind you. you turn and see a figure with eyes like flame. you fall down as if dead. what does he do?
o: tells you to stand up and be brave.
lays his right hand on you and says fear not.
games.why: "he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last." the hand that holds the stars rests on a frightened man.

practice: Name one thing you're afraid of at the moment, quietly, without arguing with it, then imagine a hand laid on you, warm and steady, as in the vision.
If you pray, let the words come: Fear not; I am the first and the last; if not, just notice the steadiness of the hand. Each time the fear comes back, feel the hand again.
